She was married to al-Mundhir ibn al-Zubayr, a marriage her father initially rejected on returning to Medina, and had children including Abd al-Rahman, Ibrahim and Qurayba.

research_evidence: Identified as Hafsa bint Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, a Medinan tabi'iyya rated ثقة (trustworthy), niece of Aisha; no death year stated on the page.

bio: A Medinan Ansari narrator of the Khazraj, of the third generation (tabaqa). Ibn Hajar rated him trustworthy, al-Dhahabi authenticated him, and al-'Ijli called him a Medinan tabi'i and thiqa. bio: A Basran tabi'i rated trustworthy (thiqa) whose transmission appears in Sahih Muslim. He was known for continuous fasting: sources say 'Khulaid al-Asari used to fast perpetually.' The page gives his death as 91 AH, with alternative reports placing it between 101 and 110 AH.

bio: A Hadrami jurist who served as qadi in Barqa and then Egypt from 120 AH, moved to official correspondence duties in 127 AH, and returned to the judiciary in 133 AH before withdrawing in 135 AH and declining reappointment. He was fluent in Coptic and held separate sessions after the afternoon prayer to settle disputes among Christians. A contemporary said he never met a judge of Egypt more learned in fiqh than Khayr ibn Nu'aym.
research_evidence: توفي ١٣٧ هـ (Died 137 AH / 754 CE)

bio: A Hijazi narrator of the Aslam tribe, of the fifth generation according to al-Taqrib. Ibn Hajar rated him 'maqbul' (acceptable) while al-Dhahabi declared him trustworthy, and Ibn Hibban listed him in his Kitab al-Thiqat. He transmitted the account of his grandfather Hazzal al-Aslami, and scholars debated whether he heard directly from Jabir ibn Abdullah.
research_evidence: Shamela narrator entry for Yazid ibn Nu'aym ibn Hazzal al-Aslami: death year given as 120 AH; fifth generation (tabaqa) of narrators according to al-Taqrib.

Hadith critics uniformly weakened him: al-Nasa'i called him matruk (abandoned), al-Bukhari munkar al-hadith, and Ibn Hibban accused him of transmitting fabricated reports. Ibn Sa'd notes he was dignified and eloquent but kept singing slave girls, which damaged his standing.

bio: An Egyptian narrator whom Yahya bin Ma'in graded thiqa. Ibn Hibban noted he belonged to the clan of the Companion Ruwayfi' bin Thabit al-Balawi and was among those who sat in his company.
research_evidence: شييم بن بيتان، من أهل مصر، ثقة (no death year stated on page; our record also has no death year; the unique name and Egyptian Qitbani/Balawi affiliation match)
dod_s: c. 723 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

students: Yahya bin Ayoub bin Abi Zara' al-Bajli
bio: An Egyptian Follower originally associated with Jayshan in Yemen, named Dailam (or, per one source, Ubayd ibn Shurhabil). Medieval scholars noted confusion in some chains between this Follower al-Jayshani and a similarly named Companion (al-Jushami) in the hadith about intoxicating drinks.
research_evidence: No death year stated on the page. Identity evidence: 'a man from the Followers from the people of Egypt' — given name Dylam (ديلم), one source gives 'Ubayd ibn Shurhabil (عبيد بن شرحبيل), kunya Abu Wahb (أبو وهب).
dod_s: c. 733 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

hadith_narrated.url: http://qaalaRasulAllah.com/hadith.php?ID=2&Rows=1&SID=17018&head=Sunan Abi Da'ud [Narrated by Hameed al-Shamy al-Hmsy حميد الشامي الحمصي]

bio: An obscure Syrian narrator from Homs about whom the rijal scholars said little was known. He appears essentially as the sole transmitter of a hadith from Sulayman al-Minbahi concerning the Prophet's covenant with his family; his hadith was recorded by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah.
research_evidence: No death year stated in the Tahdhib al-Kamal entry titled حميد الشامي الحمصي (Humayd al-Shami al-Himsi). Identity evidence: entry names him as narrating from Sulayman al-Minbahi (سليمان المنبهي); assessment quoted: 'عدم وضوح مكانته بين الرواة' (lack of clarity regarding his position among narrators).
dod_s: c. 743 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

students: Abu Bakr bin 'Abdullah bin Abi Maryum
bio: A Syrian (Bilad al-Sham) Follower and hadith transmitter graded thiqa (trustworthy). He transmitted reports attributed to the Prophet through interrupted chains (irsal). His death is placed at 101 AH, with some sources giving a range of 101-110 AH.
research_evidence: Death year stated: '١٠١ هـ (٧١٩م)' — 101 AH (719 CE); the entry also notes a range of 101-110 AH.

bio: A Syrian Follower described in the sources as both Damascene and Himsi, brother of the Umayyad governor 'Adi ibn Artah al-Fazari; one source notes Zayd was greater and more ascetic than his brother. Graded trustworthy by al-'Ijli and included in Ibn Hibban's al-Thiqat; some of his reports are mursal, and sources mention narration from Abu al-Darda and Abu Umama.
research_students: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir
research_evidence: No death year stated on the page. Identity evidence: Zayd ibn Artah al-Fazari, tabi'i, brother of 'Adi ibn Artah al-Fazari; graded 'thiqah' by al-'Ijli, 'la ba'sa bihi' by Abu Hatim, listed in Ibn Hibban's al-Thiqat.
dod_s: c. 743 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الواحد بن قيس السلمي أبو حمزة
bio: A Damascene narrator whose grading varied sharply: al-Bukhari counted him among reliable narrators, while Abu Hatim said 'his reports are recorded but he is not strong' and Ibn Hibban noted he transmitted anomalous reports (manakir). He served as teacher to the children of the Umayyad caliph Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik and reportedly declined payment for Qur'anic instruction.
research_evidence: No death year stated on the page. Identity evidence: عبد الواحد بن قيس السلمي, 'من أهل دمشق' (from the people of Damascus), kunya given in a related entry as 'أبو حمزة الدمشقي' (Abu Hamza al-Dimashqi); narrated from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr and Nafi'.
dod_s: c. 743 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

famous: 'Ali bin Yazid bin Abi Hilal al-Alhani
full: 'Ali bin Yazid bin Abi Hilal al-Alhani
full_name_ar: علي بن يزيد بن أبي هلال الألهاني
students: Yazid bin Sinan bin Yazid al-Tamimi
bio: A Damascene narrator of the sixth generation, kunya Abu Abd al-Malik (also called Abu al-Hasan). The rijal scholars overwhelmingly graded him weak: Ibn Hajar said 'da'if', al-Bukhari 'munkar al-hadith', and al-Nasa'i, al-Daraqutni and others 'matruk' (abandoned). Ibn Adi noted the problem lay partly with weak narrators reporting from him rather than defects in him directly.
research_evidence: Death year explicitly stated: 'تاريخ الوفاة: 110 هـ' (date of death: 110 AH); tabaqa: الطبقة السادسة (sixth generation).
dod_s: c. 728 CE (converted from 110 AH)

bio: A Damascene ascetic narrator known as Abu Abd Rabb al-Zahid (also written Abu Abd Rabbih or Abu Abd Rabb al-Izza), a mawla whose given name is disputed in the sources. He narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and Ibn Majah transmitted two of his hadiths. He died in 112 AH during the caliphate of Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik.
research_students: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir
research_evidence: 'مات في ولاية هشام بن عبد الملك سنة اثنتي عشرة ومئة قبل الجراح' — died during the rule of Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik in the year 112 AH, before al-Jarrah (per Mu'awiyah ibn Salih al-Dimashqi).
dod_s: c. 730 CE (converted from 112 AH)

hadith_narrated.url: http://qaalaRasulAllah.com/hadith.php?ID=2&Rows=1&SID=18034&head=Sunan Abi Da'ud [Narrated by Aslm al-Mnqry Abu Sa'id Hdythh أسلم المنقري]

bio: A narrator with the kunya Abu Sa'id, graded trustworthy (thiqa) by both Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Yahya ibn Ma'in, though both admitted they did not know his hometown or origin. He transmitted from major Followers such as Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, and Sufyan al-Thawri was among those who narrated from him.
research_teachers: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza
research_evidence: 'died in the year 142 AH' (سنة اثنتين وأربعين ومئة).
dod_s: c. 759 CE (converted from 142 AH)

students: Abu Bakr bin 'Abdullah bin Abi Maryum

hadith_narrated.url: http://qaalaRasulAllah.com/hadith.php?ID=2&Rows=1&SID=18090&head=Sunan Abi Da'ud [Narrated by Bilal bin Abi al-Drda'a بلال بن أبي الدرداء الأنصاري]

bio: Son of the Companion Abu al-Darda. He served as judge of Damascus, holding the judiciary after al-Nu'man ibn Bashir until the caliph Abd al-Malik replaced him; al-Bukhari even calls him 'amir of al-Sham'. He narrated from his father Abu al-Darda and from Umm al-Darda, and al-Dhahabi notes he was older than Umm al-Darda al-Sughra.
research_evidence: 'وقال أبو عبيد: مات سنة ثلاث وتسعين' — Abu Ubayd said: he died in the year 93 (AH).
dod_s: c. 712 CE (converted from 93 AH)
